subtopic: Using AI tools inside a team
subtype: Approach: protecting skills and learning of juniors [Thinking]
passage: With a client demo two days away and the office loud from renovation drilling, Avni still stopped at Minakshi's desk. Minakshi, a junior developer, had been pasting tasks into an AI tool and getting answers before reading the ticket. Avni worried Minakshi would reach the second year without knowing how the code worked. Over the drilling she said, 'New rule for juniors. Try it yourself first, even if it's rough. Then ask the tool to review it. And afterwards explain the code to me in your own words.' Minakshi frowned. 'That's slower.' 'A bit,' said Avni, 'but you'll be the one fixing it at midnight, not the tool.' They agreed to test it on one ticket that afternoon. The first attempt was clumsy, the review found two problems, and the explanation took ten minutes and showed one gap.

qa.q: What was making the office loud?
qa.a: Renovation drilling was making the office loud.
Avni is worried that Minakshi would reach the second year without knowing how the code works.

qa.q: What other approach could Avni add to protect the juniors' learning?
qa.a: Avni could set up a weekly walkthrough where each junior explains one piece of their code to a senior, since explaining out loud shows gaps quickly.

qa.q: How might Minakshi see the new rule?
qa.a: Minakshi found it slower and frowned, though the review and the explanation exposed a gap that may show its worth.

grounding: Shows a lead worried that juniors will stop learning fundamentals, so asking them to try first, use AI for review and explain their code.

subtopic: Using AI tools inside a team
subtype: Approach: protecting skills and learning of juniors [Thinking]
passage:
In the Noida office, Tushar noticed that Vikas, his newest developer, could finish tasks quickly but went blank when asked why the code worked. The pull requests were clean; the explanations were not.
Tushar thought about it on the metro home. If juniors let the tool do all the thinking, in two years they'd be fast but unable to debug anything new. He didn't want to ban the tool; it did help.
Next morning he told Vikas and the other two juniors: 'New rule for three months. First, try the task yourself for an hour. Then ask the AI to review your attempt. Then, in the pull request, explain the final code in your own words, three lines.'
Vikas's first explanation was clumsy. By the fourth week, he caught a bug the AI had missed.

qa.q: How long should the juniors try a task themselves first?
What was Tushar worried about on the metro home?
qa.a: Tushar was worried that juniors relying on the tool would become fast but unable to debug anything new.

qa.q: What else could Tushar do to support the juniors' learning?
qa.a: He could pair each junior with a senior for one debugging session a week, so they see how problems are reasoned through.

qa.q: How might Vikas experience the new rule?
qa.a: At first it feels slower and clumsy, but by the fourth week Vikas gains the confidence of catching a bug the AI missed.

grounding: It shows a lead worried that juniors will stop learning fundamentals asking them to attempt tasks first, then use AI for review and explain the code in their own words.

'Mohit, walk me through this function,' Shreya said, pointing at his screen.
'It... sorts the orders by date, and then... the AI wrote this part.'
'What does this part do?'
Mohit scrolled. 'I'm not sure, honestly.'
Shreya leaned back. 'That's what worries me. Not the tool. You. If you can't explain it, you can't fix it at 3 a.m.'
'So I shouldn't use it?'
'Use it. Differently. For the next few months: you write the first version yourself, even if it's ugly. Then ask the AI to review it. Then you explain the final code to me in your own words, before merging.'
'That'll take longer.'
'For now. Then you'll be faster than both of us.'
Mohit laughed a little and closed the AI window. 'Okay. Ugly version first.'

qa.q: What does Shreya want Mohit to write first?
qa.a: The first version, himself, even if it's ugly.

qa.q: How does Mohit feel when he can't explain the code?
qa.a: He feels embarrassed and unsure, admitting honestly that he doesn't know what that part does.

qa.q: What else could help Mohit learn the fundamentals?
qa.a: He could keep a short note of each idea he had to look up, and go over it with Shreya each week.

qa.q: How does the new approach look to Shreya?
qa.a: Shreya sees it as protecting Mohit's growth, worth a slower start so he can later fix problems on his own.

grounding: It shows a lead who worries juniors will stop learning asking a junior to attempt tasks first, use the AI for review and explain the code in his own words.
